In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the glucocorticoid hormone cortisol on the synthesis of fatty acids in the perfused livers of adrenalectoized rats, using 3H2o as the tracer.
the effects of the adrenalectomy and cortisol on the hepatic lipogenesis and the desaturation of newly synthesized fatty acids, in fed and starved rats.
the effects of adrenalectomy and cortisol administration on the synthesis of fatty acids in the perfused rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adrenalectomy impairs hepatic lipogenesis by a defect in desaturation of fatty acids and by an impairment in the export of newly synthesized saturated fatty acids from the liver.
adrenalectomy impairs hepatic fatty acid synthesis in vivo, and that this impairment is corrected by glucocorticoids.

the impairment of hepatic lipogenesis after adrenalectomization in non-diabetic rats is due to a decrease in the capacity for fatty acid biosynthesis, and is not due to a defect in the uptake and/or metabolism of precursors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adrenal cortex is a major determinant of the rate of hepatic lipogenesis.
the adrenal glucocorticoid hormone is a necessary factor in maintaining the capacity of the liver to synthesize fatty acids from glucose.
adrenalectomy reduces the capacity of the liver for fatty acid synthesis and desaturations, but does not impair the utilization of fatty acids for glyceride synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is a major site of fatty acid synthesis, which is a key step in the process of fat accumulation.
the adrenal glands have a significant effect on the liver.
the adrenals have a role in regulating hepatic lipogenesis.
